title: Finite limits of internal abelian groups are created on underlying objects
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a category with finite limits [def-galois-finite-limits-colimits]. Write $\operatorname{AbObj}(\mathcal C)$ for the category whose objects are quadruples $(M,m,e,i)$, with $m:M\times M\to M$, $e:*\to M$ and $i:M\to M$ satisfying associativity, commutativity, the two unit laws and the inverse laws as equations of morphisms; here $*$ is terminal and products have the meaning of [def-weil-category-product]. Morphisms preserve these operations. Let $U_{\mathcal C}:\operatorname{AbObj}(\mathcal C)\to\mathcal C$ forget the operations.

For every finite category $I$, every diagram $D:I\to\operatorname{AbObj}(\mathcal C)$ and every limiting cone $(L,(p_j)_j)$ of $U_{\mathcal C}D$, there is exactly one abelian-group-object structure on the same object $L$ making all $p_j$ group-object morphisms. With this structure the cone is limiting in $\operatorname{AbObj}(\mathcal C)$: the unique underlying factorization of any group-object cone is a group-object morphism. Moreover, a cone of group objects is limiting if and only if its underlying cone is limiting. Thus $U_{\mathcal C}$ creates, preserves and reflects finite limits, including the empty limit.

Let $\mathcal D$ also have finite limits, and let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ preserve finite limits. Equip $FM$ with $F(m)\circ\lambda_{M,M}^{-1}$, $F(e)\circ\lambda_*^{-1}$ and $F(i)$, where $\lambda_{M,N}:F(M\times N)\to FM\times FN$ and $\lambda_*:F(*)\to *$ are the canonical comparisons. This operation transport, with $h\mapsto F(h)$ on morphisms, defines a functor $F^{\mathrm{ab}}:\operatorname{AbObj}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{AbObj}(\mathcal D)$, and $F^{\mathrm{ab}}$ preserves finite limits.
